key_insight: Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) recovers correlation lost during stabilizer projection, improving quantum chemistry accuracy without enlarging the retained quantum register.
engineering_relevance: SSPT can help resource-constrained quantum chemistry workflows reach chemical precision with fewer contextual qubits.
method: Use Pauli terms eliminated by stabilizer projection to generate external states from an optimized CS-VQE reference.
Estimate energy corrections with Epstein–Nesbet-type second-order perturbation theory or an external-space resolvent.
Evaluate required matrix elements through reduced-register Pauli expectation values, avoiding full-space wave-function reconstruction.
evidence_signal: Molecular benchmarks report substantial reductions in projection-induced energy errors and chemical precision with fewer contextual qubits in several cases; the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify measurement overhead or external-space scaling, leaving the total resource trade-off uncertain.
paper_title: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry
